blocks.text: What an AI assistant for interior designers does on your Mac

Lazur lives in the notch at the top of your Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘, ask about anything on your screen, and it answers out loud. It sees the screen while you hold the keys, so you do not have to describe the drawing or the email to it. That matters when a supplier message sits in one window and your spec sheet sits in another.

That is a different job from a design tool. SketchUp, Figma and Photoshop still do the drawing. Lazur helps with the work around the drawing. It finds the right control, explains a number, drafts the email that goes with a revision and reminds you about the call. It does not take the mouse. Every click stays yours.
Where an interior designer's week goes

Start with what the research supports. The Bureau of Labor Statistics says most interior designers use computer-aided design software for most of their drawings. The same handbook lists bidding on new projects, estimating project costs and placing material orders as duties. It also says designers may meet clients in the evening and on weekends. Drawing is one part of that list, not the whole list.

Hours are the next question. A Houzz Pro survey from 2022 found that 59% of the designers it surveyed work 31 to 50 hours a week. Another 30% work fewer than 30 hours, and 11% work more than 50. Houzz Pro's article says a full-time designer works 8 to 10 hours a day. The survey comes from a software company's own users, so it may lean toward firm and small business designers. It does not break hours down by task, so it cannot show where the time goes.
Why email and client messages take a bigger share than you expect

Microsoft's Work Trend Index for 2023 surveyed 31,000 full-time workers in 31 markets. It found that the average employee spends 57% of their time communicating in meetings, email and chat. Email alone is 15%. The heaviest email users, the top 25%, spend 8.8 hours a week on it. These figures cover knowledge workers in general. They are not designer data, so use them as a rough guide.

A design blog cites a 2019 Adobe study that puts office workers at 209 minutes a day checking and responding to work email. That number is secondhand here. The original study was not opened for this page. Treat it as a hint about scale, not a measure of your own inbox.

This is where a voice assistant earns its place. Hold fn and dictate a client update straight into the reply box. Dictation writes clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. You can save snippets and add words to a personal dictionary. Clipboard slots hold the sentences you type every week, such as your standard lead time wording.

For longer replies, ask Lazur to draft from the thread on screen. Read the draft first. Check every date, price and name against your own notes. Then send it yourself. In Gmail in a browser, ⌘ Return sends the message. For attachments, see [how to attach a file in Gmail](/how-to/attach-a-file-in-gmail).
Worked example: a supplier delay on a Monday morning

Say the upholsterer emails on Monday morning. The fabric is late, and you have a client call late in the afternoon. A voice assistant can carry the admin around the problem. You still make the decision. Here is one way the morning can run.

items: Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask what the upholsterer said. Lazur reads the thread on screen and summarizes the delay out loud.
Ask Lazur to research the alternative fabrics. It runs in its own Chrome tabs and returns a summary with links.
Hold fn and dictate your notes on the delay. Dictation types them at the cursor.
Ask Lazur to draft the update to the client. Read it, change the wording and send it yourself.
Ask Lazur to set a reminder in Apple Reminders for the call. You can do that by voice.

blocks.text: Each step gives you material. None of them makes the call for you. The research shows what other suppliers list. You choose the fabric. Before you promise a date to the client, check the lead time on the supplier's own site. A summary from a research job is a starting point, not a source you quote.
SketchUp, Figma and Photoshop: what Lazur can and cannot do there

SketchUp's requirements page is the most checkable source for this job. It lists macOS 27, 26 and 15 for Mac. It asks for at least 6 GB of free disk space. SketchUp 2027.0 and later need Apple silicon to install on macOS. Intel Macs can no longer install SketchUp from 2027.0. Check your chip before you update, not after the install fails.

Figma's help page for installing the desktop app does not mention macOS or Apple silicon. Check Figma's own requirements before you plan a Mac upgrade around them. Adobe's Photoshop requirements page did not open during our check, so look at Adobe's site directly for the current list.

Lazur works with what is on your screen in any app. It is not a plugin or add-in for SketchUp, Figma or Photoshop. It has no partnership with any of their makers. Ask where a control lives, and Lazur circles the button and labels it. Then you click. Lazur does not click for you.

Hand over the search, the first draft, the reminder and the plain English reading of a clause you do not follow. Then check that reading against your firm's contract template.
Client data, your firm's rules and what Lazur does with screenshots

Interior design work involves client names, home addresses, budgets and floor plans. Your firm may set rules for what goes into an AI tool. Follow them first. If there is no rule, ask before you hold the shortcut over a client file. Your duty to the client comes before any speed you gain.

Here is what Lazur does with your data. It listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. This page does not claim any compliance certification.
Before you hold the shortcut on client work, run through this list.

items: Close tabs with client bank details or ID that the task does not need.
Check your firm's policy on AI tools and client files.
Show Lazur the window you need, not your whole desktop.
Ask about the task, not the client's personal details, when you can.
Ask the client before you share anything they sent you in confidence.

blocks.text: Mistakes people make with AI on client work

Three mistakes come up often. The first is treating a summary as a source. The second is sending a draft you have not read. The third is asking one long question when three short ones would work better. A short question gets a clear answer. A long question gets a long answer that is hard to check.

A fourth mistake sits in the numbers. A rough cost from a chat answer is not a quote. Check each line against the supplier's own price list. Use the research as a lead, then open the page yourself and read the figure there.
Older Macs, Intel chips and graphics requirements

Check your Mac before you plan a SketchUp update. SketchUp's page says the new graphics engine needs Metal 2 support. Intel HD Graphics 5000 and 6000, and Intel Iris, Iris 6100 and Iris Pro, are not supported. SketchUp also no longer supports Mac devices from 2019 or earlier. Check this before a client deadline, not during one.

Lazur is for the Mac, on Apple silicon and Intel. Windows is planned, not available. If your studio mixes Macs and PCs, only the Macs can run Lazur for now. Plan your setup around that before you buy a new machine.

Ask whether anyone else uses the Mac you work on. Lazur keeps memory of what you asked and did, on that Mac. On a shared machine, think about who might open that history before you hand the computer over.
Pricing, the trial and how to start

Lazur has a Pro trial that starts the first time you open the app. No credit card is needed. After the trial, Pro and Power plans come with monthly and annual prices. Dictation is unlimited on both. Check the [pricing page](/pricing) for current prices, because they can change.

Start with one job, not the whole week. Pick the email you dread most, or the supplier question you keep putting off. Use Lazur for that task for a full working day. Then decide whether it saved you time. You can [download Lazur](/download) for the Mac from the download page.

If you work mostly in Figma, read [Figma for interior designers on Mac](/for/interior-designers/figma). For the image and rendering side, see [Photoshop for interior designers on Mac](/for/interior-designers/photoshop). faq.question: Is Lazur an AI assistant for interior designers that draws for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It sees your screen, points at controls, explains what it sees, answers out loud and drafts text. It does not draw floor plans, create renders or click buttons for you.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside SketchUp, Figma and Photoshop?
faq.answer: It works with what is on your screen in any app, because it looks at the screen while you hold ⌥ ⌘. It is not a plugin or add-in for those apps, and it has no partnership with their makers.

faq.question: Can I use it for client email?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask it to draft a reply from the thread on screen. Then read, change and send the message yourself. Dictation with fn also types text at the cursor in any app.

faq.question: Can I share client addresses or budgets with Lazur?
faq.answer: Follow your firm's rules on client data first. Lazur sends audio and the screenshot to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. This page does not claim any compliance certification.

faq.question: Does Lazur run on Intel Macs?
faq.answer: Lazur supports Macs with Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available yet. Check the download page for the latest platform details before you install.

faq.question: How does background research work?
faq.answer: Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. Open the sources it lists before you quote a price or a lead time to a client.

faq.question: Does it remember my earlier questions?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur keeps memory of what you asked and did, and that memory stays on your Mac. If other people share the computer, think about that before you use it.

faq.question: Is my screen recorded all the time?
faq.answer: No. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Once you let go, it stops.

faq.question: How do I start?
faq.answer: Download the app from the download page. The Pro trial starts the first time you open the app, and no credit card is needed. Check the pricing page for current plan prices before you choose a plan.

faq.question: Can it show me where a tool is in an app I rarely use?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where the tool is. Lazur circles the control and labels it on your screen. You do the clicking.
